comedians.name: Abby Govindan
comedians.profile_html:
In August 2026, during an Edinburgh Fringe run, The Guardian reviewed Pushing 30, Abby Govindan’s hour about love, big tech, marriage pressure, misinformation, and patriarchal expectations. “Patriarchy is not just a south Asian problem,” she says. The review called her delivery easygoing, conversational, and heartfelt.

Govindan grew up in Houston and made her comedy debut at Caroline’s on Broadway in December 2017, at 20. Her official biography puts Indian American family life, internet virality, and the pursuit of stand-up at the center of her early work.

She has folded screenshots, pranks, and PowerPoint-style visuals into story-driven stand-up. She once convinced social-media users and media outlets that she created Emily in Paris; her official site notes that she did not.

In 2025, Govindan appeared on Scam Goddess and Last Things First, and brought the solo Off-Broadway show How to Embarrass Your Immigrant Parents to SoHo Playhouse. In 2026, she appeared on SBS Spice.

comedians.name: Alonzo Bodden
comedians.profile_html:
In October 2026, a Zofunny Monthly post found Alonzo Bodden writing about friends’ illnesses and deaths, postponed knee surgery, and the decision to stop deferring pleasure. “I am continually, sadly reminded that life is promised to no one,” he wrote. His stand-up draws on current events, race, media, and everyday observation.

Bodden grew up in St. Albans, Queens, then spent about a decade as an airplane mechanic before training mechanics at McDonnell Douglas. Teaching made him comfortable before a room; a comedy-writing course graduation show gave him his first time onstage. He began doing stand-up in Los Angeles in 1993, at 30, and later broke through at Montreal’s Just for Laughs. “I never looked back,” he said. “I knew that this was what I was going to do.”

His delivery is conversational. The Showtime specials Who’s Paying Attention? (2011), Historically Incorrect (2016), and Heavy Lightweight (2019) were followed in 2026 by How Do You Spell Moth?, released through Dry Bar Comedy and Angel. On television, he won NBC’s third season of Last Comic Standing after finishing runner-up in season two, and played Alonzo in five 2014 episodes of Californication.

comedians.name: Anjelah Johnson-Reyes
comedians.profile_html:
In May 2026, “Ugly Baby” arrived on YouTube, Anjelah Johnson-Reyes’s seventh hour-long special and her directorial debut. Filmed over two sold-out shows at Los Angeles’s El Rey Theatre, it covers motherhood in her 40s, fertility, pregnancy, postpartum life, relationships, and family generations. The material moves through personal stories, impressions, and characters.

Raised in San Jose, California, Johnson-Reyes was an Oakland Raiderette before moving to Los Angeles in 2005. A free church joke-writing class got her into comedy; “Nail Salon” was among her first jokes. She joined MADtv in 2007, playing Mỹ Linh, Tammy, and fast-food employee Bon Qui Qui, whose “I’M A CUT YOU” became the line. Her comedy returns to extended family, marriage, motherhood, aging, and daily irritations. Netflix tagged her 2015 special “Not Fancy” as Witty and Clean-Cut.

The Family Reunion tour sold more than 200,000 tickets across more than 100 U.S. theater shows in 2025 and 2026.

Her screen work includes Curb Your Enthusiasm, Ugly Betty, Superstore, and Hulu’s Life & Beth. In May 2024, she hosted Tubi’s eight-episode My Crazy Quince.

shows.name: Funjelah Live Podcast Taping w/ Anjelah Johnson-Reyes & Special Guest

comedians.name: Chris Fleming
comedians.profile_html:
In August 2026, Harper’s Bazaar caught Chris Fleming after the premiere of Chris Fleming: Live at the Palace, his HBO and HBO Max special, and his first Emmy nomination for Outstanding Writing for a Variety Special. “That special was me firing at the height of my powers,” he said.

Fleming grew up in Stow, Massachusetts, in an Irish Catholic family. New England, suburban social types, therapy, consumer culture, and performance anxiety recur in his work. His early online breakthrough was Gayle, the web series about Gayle Waters-Waters, a hyper-competitive suburban mother.

His stand-up mixes stories, dancing, songs, and sketch-like framing with strenuous physical performance. Harper’s Bazaar described him as constantly in motion onstage; Marc Maron called the act unusually free and improvisationally flexible. The 2018 YouTube special Showpig came before the 2023 Peacock special Chris Fleming: Hell.

Fleming played Leonard in the 2025 Abbott Elementary episode “Karaoke.” In March 2026, he appeared on Late Night with Seth Meyers to promote Live at the Palace.

comedians.name: Chrissy Chlapecka
comedians.profile_html:
In June 2026, “Christine: High Voltage” arrived as the 16-track second act to Chrissy Chlapecka’s 2025 project Christine. In a June 2026 Hollywood Rebound interview, she framed the releases in theater-kid terms: “Act One” and “Act Two.”

Chicago-born Chlapecka built a TikTok following with a hyper-feminine bimbo persona and commentary on queer identity, misogyny, and self-confidence. “I don’t do this for the misogynistic male gaze... I do it for my gaze, and damn! My tits look good!” she has said. Her short-form work favors characters and sociopolitical commentary over conventional stand-up premises.

Music and musical theater were central to her upbringing before TikTok became pivotal to her career. Her 2024 debut EP, Girlie Pop, took its name from her own definition: “For me, Girlie Pop is a subgenre of music that I have created based on my own experiences and love for girly, fun, campy, cheeky self-love music that makes you wanna dance.” She also appeared on Craig & Friends in 2021.

Live, Chlapecka turns the material into a colorful, theatrical, vocal-forward pop show for a predominantly queer audience.

comedians.name: Clint Coley
comedians.profile_html:
In September 2026, on 1-on-1’s w/Deuces, Clint Coley discussed a comedy tour, Savage X Fenty, and the World Series of Spades. His stand-up draws on Philadelphia, dating, sex, and gender dynamics. It is candid, blunt, and high-energy.

In an Okayplayer interview, Coley described the routine of managing his bipolar diagnosis: “It takes a while to wrap your head around the fact that you gotta take meds every single day. You have to do it. Like, ain't no you skipped your meds like four or five days.”

Coley appeared on the inaugural 2022 episode of D.L. Hughley’s Speakeasy: Comedy Overload and on podcasts including Rent’s Due, which follows the development of his next special. He created and produced the World Series of Spades, and wrote and starred in the 2016 short film The First Date.

comedians.name: Daniel Sloss
comedians.profile_html:
In July 2026, The List found Daniel Sloss discussing two sitcoms in development after time away from touring following the birth of his daughter in 2024. “One is about an angry Scottish comedian. The other is about being an angry Scottish person in America.”

Sloss began writing and performing in 2007 after his mother met Frankie Boyle at a conference. Boyle gave him early access to the comedy circuit. He made his Edinburgh Fringe stand-up debut in 2008, aged 17. His shows have since traveled through 55 countries and nine New York off-Broadway seasons.

The 2018 Netflix specials DARK and Jigsaw cover the death of his sister, Josie, and relationships. In 2019’s Daniel Sloss: X, he addresses gender expectations, toxic masculinity, and the sexual assault of a close friend. The structure often starts provocative or slapstick, then turns toward personal reflection.

Later releases include SOCIO in 2022, HUBRiS in 2024, and CAN’T, released on DanielSloss.com in December 2025. He has also appeared ten times on Conan, according to his official biography.

comedians.name: Dave Chappelle
comedians.profile_html:
In August 2026, the Associated Press reported that Dave Chappelle was scheduled to host Lauryn Hill’s Diaspora Calling! festival.

Born in Washington, D.C., Dave Chappelle split time between the Washington area and Yellow Springs, Ohio, after his parents separated. He attended Duke Ellington School of the Arts and moved to New York in 1991 for the stand-up club circuit, as outlined in his career background. He starred in the 1996 sitcom Buddies, then co-created and starred in Comedy Central’s Chappelle’s Show, which premiered in 2003.

Dave Chappelle builds long anecdotes from personal experience and cultural observation, covering race and racism in the United States, American politics, fatherhood and celebrity culture. Netflix released The Dreamer in 2023. His other specials include 2017’s The Age of Spin and Equanimity, 2019’s Sticks & Stones, and 2021’s The Closer.

comedians.name: Desi Banks
comedians.profile_html:
In April 2026, Forbes caught up with Desi Banks as he leaned into his “Your Favorite Cousin” identity and prepared for the forthcoming film Boyz Trip. “I look at myself as a comedian, not just a social media comedian,” he said.

Raised on Atlanta’s east side, Banks began posting sketches on Vine in 2012 and started doing stand-up in 2017. His background includes Cedar Grove High School, college football at Morehead State and Georgia State, and a sociology degree earned in December 2015.

Banks played Fonk the Freak in a 2022 episode of Sherman’s Showcase, appeared on Season 6 of The Shop: Uninterrupted in 2023, and joined Ms. Pat on a 2025 episode of We Got Time Today.

He has described the stage as a proving ground. Once the audience is with him, he can be freer with the material.

comedians.name: Dovi Neuburger
comedians.profile_html:
Dovi Neuburger draws on yeshiva culture, family expectations, faith, and dating, adjusting the context for audiences less familiar with Jewish practice. A September 2026 Unpacked profile noted his effort to bring Orthodox Jewish comedy beyond its usual audience. One early joke he counted as a major success used “Love on the Spectrum” as a misdirection after a premise about Jewish dating.

Neuburger left NYU Law after one semester and first tried stand-up at a Hanukkah show at Young Israel of the Upper West Side. He nearly quit after bombing. Then came a successful Purim set at Stand Up NY in March 2023, followed by a Gotham Comedy Club class, open mics, and more shows. His material includes his father’s criticism of a mezuzah’s placement in his apartment and the difficulty of getting a blanket into a duvet cover.

His official site says he regularly opens Elon Gold’s theater dates and founded and produces the StandUp for Israel Comedy Tour. On BrainStorm with Sony Perlman in 2024, Neuburger discussed leaving law school. In 2026, he appeared on AND HERE’S MODI to discuss a seven-show Israel run, the matchmaker process, a Birthright trip, and being a rabbi’s son.

For live rooms, Neuburger adjusts the cultural explanation without sanding down the specifics. Ami Kozak told Unpacked that he brings “proper standup insight to the Jewish world” and makes specificity feel universal.

comedians.name: Ellen Skrmetti
comedians.profile_html:
Cattywampus: A Southern Woman’s Guide to Laughing When Life Goes Sideways is Ellen Skrmetti’s second essay collection from Apiary, following 2024’s Hey, Jesus, It’s Me: I Have Questions, Comments, and Concerns.

Skrmetti started performing stand-up in 2020 after taking comedy-writing classes at 41. When live comedy paused during the pandemic, she took online classes with Second City and made character sketches, including “If the Queen Died in the South,” before building out “Hey Jesus, It’s Me.”

Her clean, faith-inflected Southern comedy covers marriage, motherhood, menopause, college football, and Southern culture. “I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me. What if I don’t want to?” Her work pairs personal-storytelling stand-up with short, character-driven social-media sketches.

She appeared on That Sounds Fun with Annie F. Downs in 2024 and In Good Faith in September 2025. WSFA 12 News interviewed her in October 2024 about Hey Jesus, It’s Me.

comedians.name: FOOS GONE WILD
comedians.profile_html:
In July 2026, will.i.am’s video for “SICK ASS FOO’S”, featuring Lil Mr. E and Toxica, credited “Original Music: will.i.am & FOOS GONE WILD.”

FOOS GONE WILD began as an Instagram account in 2018, built on user-submitted photos and videos, captions, high-pitched voice-over commentary, original animations, and music. A 2019 L.A. TACO profile described the anonymous operation as a collective connected to Tijuana, Los Angeles, San Diego, and Oxnard. Its working definition: “A foo is a foo, you just know one when you see one.”

Lowriders, party lines, West Coast rap, G-funk, tube socks, Cortez shoes, and the social taxonomy of the foo recur. Drug slang comes with anti-drug disclaimers. “The Higher The Socks (The Downer The Foo).”

Lil Mr. E told L.A. TACO in 2020 that the project combined comedy, cartoons, and music. The 16-track WELCOME TO FOOVILLE arrived in June 2026.

comedians.name: Iván Fematt La Mole
comedians.profile_html:
“Qué necesidad de ir a un reality show a que te humillen, te critiquen y te insulten”. In an October 7, 2026, post reported the next day by POSTA México, Iván Fematt La Mole criticized the premise of entering a reality show to be humiliated, criticized or insulted. He named no program or contestant.

Iván Fematt La Mole emerged from Monterrey television and radio. On Acábatelo, he played Markitos, Empanadín, Maricela, Oso Dammy and El Guardia. He competed on Prime Video’s 2019 second season of LOL: Last One Laughing and hosts the Multimedios late-night program Buenas noches Don Fematt.

His stand-up pulls from television, newspapers, weddings and daily experience. “Voy sacando del día a día, leyendo el periódico, viendo la tele, voy a una boda y de cada vivencia saco una experiencia o un dato que voy incorporando,” he has said. The material is improvised, audience-near and rooted in Monterrey and northern Mexico. “No soy mucho de meterme con la gente,” he has also said.

At a November 2024 performance in Tijuana, Semanario ZETA reported that Iván Fematt La Mole worked with an audience of more than 1,000 people, using stories contextualized to the border audience.

comedians.name: Joanne McNally
comedians.profile_html:
Joanne McNally came to stand-up after appearing in Una McKevitt’s 2014 stage show Singlehood, following work in public relations and for a mental-health charity. Her 2016 one-woman show Bite Me drew on her experience of eating disorders. Dating, female friendship, nightlife, class and Irish identity remain in the mix. Her background supplies the stories.

Her stand-up runs on conversational riffing and quick timing. A bald man gets no evasive courtesy: “I’ll stop you there, you know you’re bald? This conversation sounds like you think you’ve got a full head of hair.” McNally also takes aim at her own background: “I do say I’m from a posh part of Dublin and then I slag them.”

On television, McNally co-hosted RTÉ2’s Republic of Telly and competed on Channel 4’s Taskmaster Series 17. She appeared on Taskmaster: The Podcast in 2024 and Off Menu in 2025.

comedians.name: Josh Blue
comedians.profile_html:
In February 2026, Colorado Public Radio spoke with Josh Blue at Boulder’s Dairy Arts Center about his first memoir, Something To Stare At. The 2025 book covers childhood in West Africa, cerebral palsy, Paralympic soccer and comedy. Blue called the project “putting the cerebral in cerebral palsy.”

Blue was born in Cameroon, raised in St. Paul, Minnesota, and started doing open mics at Evergreen State College in Olympia, Washington. He represented the United States in cerebral-palsy football at the 2004 Paralympic Games in Athens, then built a comedy career in Denver. In 2006, he won the fourth season of NBC’s Last Comic Standing. He later appeared on The Ellen DeGeneres Show and The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, and finished third on America’s Got Talent in 2021.

His material draws on single parenting, divorce, family life and strangers’ assumptions about cerebral palsy. “There’s no map on that. I’ve never written anything down physically. It’s just all kind of off the top of my head.” Freak Accident, his 2024 special, was released through YouTube and 800 Pound Gorilla Media. Earlier releases include 2012’s Josh Blue: Sticky Change on Showtime.

Blue changes the order, timing and topics as the room demands. Crowd interaction can become part of the set.

comedians.name: Josh Gondelman
comedians.profile_html:
In September 2026, the Boston Globe found Josh Gondelman working on a weekly interview podcast, larger projects with Alison Leiby, and an hour he hoped to record in spring 2027. “I didn’t start doing stand-up to become vertically integrated,” he said. Gondelman began at Boston open mics in 2004; his comedy still has the regional compression he once called “Catholicism with bagels.”

His delivery is warm and non-aggressive, or, in Gondelman’s phrase, “wide-eyed friendliness.” He likes the mechanics, the “joke math.” A Massachusetts-themed shirt becomes a ranking system: “Level three is a button-down shirt with a camo pattern made of shamrocks, and it’s called ‘shamouflage.’” Then comes the rule: “You’re really only supposed to wear it when a Dropkick Murphy is born or dies.”

Gondelman moved to New York in 2011. His official biography credits him as a former web producer and staff writer for Last Week Tonight with John Oliver, head writer and executive producer for Desus & Mero, and a contributor to the final season of The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel. It also lists appearances on Conan, Late Night with Seth Meyers, and The Late Late Show with James Corden.

His 2022 special, People Pleaser, was billed as “not-quite-clean but very friendly.” The 2025 YouTube special Positive Reinforcement followed. He also appeared on Hey Riddle Riddle in 2026.

comedians.name: Karen Morgan
comedians.profile_html:
In 2026, Angel began streaming Put Some Butter On It, Karen Morgan’s third Dry Bar Comedy special. Angel describes it this way: “Karen Morgan believes brides who give dress codes for guests should have their weddings ruined.” Her material covers parenting, marriage, aging and generational differences.

Karen Morgan began her professional comedy career in 2005, after taking a local comedy workshop while raising three children. A tape sent to Nickelodeon’s Search for the Funniest Mom in America made her one of seven finalists from more than 1,000 applicants. She earned a BFA from the University of Georgia in 1986 and practiced as a trial attorney, a background documented in her University of Georgia profile.

Her 2023 YouTube special Glamour Shots In The Dark includes chapters called “Cassette Tape,” “Perilous Playground,” and “Mean Candy.” Earlier Dry Bar specials include Go Dawgs! from 2020 and Rub Some Dirt On It from 2023. In May 2024, she performed on The Talk’s “Stand Up at THE TALK” segment.

shows.name: Comedian Karen Morgan (Dry Bar Comedy) Live in Conroe

comedians.name: Keegan Tindall
comedians.profile_html:
In September 2026, CBS aired Keegan Tindall on “Comics Unleashed with Byron Allen”, alongside Luenell, CJ Marrinan, and Michael Turner. His work includes stand-up and original online sketches with a playful, absurd streak.

Tindall is from South Jersey and based in New York. On Robert Kelly’s September 2024 “You Know What Dude?” appearance, “Eating Dog Food,” he discussed being burned after a drunk driver hit him, his family, and his father’s habit of eating dog food. A 2023 appearance on “Mindful Metal Jacket” carried the subtitle “Burn Victim Guy.”

The New York Comedy Festival named him a Comic to Watch in 2024. Moontower Comedy notes that he was passed at the Comedy Cellar. In November 2025, he wrote and voiced the comedy animation “Gnome Bacon.”

Keegan Tindall Headlines The Riot Comedy Club

comedians.name: Kev Adams
comedians.profile_html:
In September 2026, discussing La Maison de nos rêves with France Inter, Kev Adams said: “Je crois que l'on écrit ce que l'on est.” The film, directed by Claude Zidi Jr. and released in French cinemas in October 2026, was co-written by Adams, who also stars in it. He linked its portrayal of loneliness among older people to personal experience.

Adams gained wider exposure in 2009 through opening appearances connected with Anne Roumanoff and Gad Elmaleh. His first solo show was billed as The Young Man Show. The material draws on love, success and social commentary. His official show history includes the Olympia, Zénith venues and Accor Arena.

On screen, Adams starred in and co-created Soda, the French short-format comedy series. He was a panelist on TF1’s Mask Singer from 2019 through 2026. His 2022 Netflix special, Kev Adams: The Real Me, is a standalone set. In 2026, he performed a stand-up audition in English on America’s Got Talent.

comedians.name: Luke Kidgell
comedians.profile_html:
Luke Kidgell started performing stand-up in 2015 after seeing Nick Cody at that year’s Comedy Festival. Three months later, he tried it himself, he told The Western Weekender. He had already been posting videos to Instagram and YouTube before clips from live sets widened his audience on TikTok. “Sometimes people just scream the word ‘TikTok’ at me,” he has said. “They’ll just yell the platform that they know me from.”

Kidgell mixes prepared material with anecdotes and audience interaction. Travel, touring, awkward encounters and everyday observations are all in the rotation. He calls the approach “silly, interactive, and hopefully funny.” “I just like talking to people and seeing what happens on the night,” he has said.

His YouTube specials include Cheers To That (2023) and Happy Hour (2025), filmed on his 2024 UK tour and released March 12, 2025. His official biography says the Happy Hour tour played to more than 150,000 people across 14 countries. He also co-hosts the B.L.T. comedy podcast with Blake Pavey and Tyler Cahill.

shows.name: Luke Kidgell - Live In The USA

comedians.name: Marito Lopez
comedians.profile_html:
In September 2026, The Secret Sex Lives of Muslim Women introduced Marito Lopez as “the first straight cis man to ever enter The Secret Sex Lives of Muslim Women.” He discussed sobriety, his conversion to Islam, faith, sex, and dating.

Lopez began performing comedy in 2009. Born in El Salvador, he immigrated to Canada with his family as a child and grew up in Calgary, Alberta. After working there, he relocated to Toronto and performed in New York City. A talent-management profile lists The Stand and New York Comedy Club among the rooms where he is a regular.

Lopez voiced Marito in 17 episodes of Gary and His Demons from 2018 to 2023, played Carlito in four 2024 episodes of One More Time, and competed on Roast Battle Canada against Jarrett Campbell and Sophie Buddle. He was featured in the March 2022 The New Wave of Standup episode devoted to him. His 2026 Apple TV special followed the February 2025 release of his comedy album LatinXXX.

comedians.name: Marlon Wayans
comedians.profile_html:
In August 2026, Real Laughs heard Marlon Wayans describe a new hour taking shape in clubs, with another special expected within months. “I stay on stage and I keep grinding and it just makes me better,” he said. His stand-up runs on physical humor, impressions, and personal stories.

Wayans has worked since his 1988 film debut in I’m Gonna Git You Sucka. He became widely known through The Wayans Bros. and the Scary Movie films. His 2018 Netflix special Marlon Wayans: Woke-ish and HBO Max’s Marlon Wayans: God Loves Me make room for family, race, relationships, fear, and his own mistakes.

That turn lands hardest in 2024’s Good Grief: “I’ve been dodging depression for the last three years. I lost my momma three years ago. And let me tell you y’all something, ain’t no pain, ain’t no nothing like losing your momma.” In a CBS News interview about grief, stand-up, and acting, he put his career drive plainly: “I don’t know if I’m chasing, or if I’m running from something!”

comedians.name: Michael Rowland
comedians.profile_html:
Michael Rowland began in stand-up. Born in Atlanta, he lives in New York City.

His 2020 Comedy Central Stand-Up Featuring set was titled “Have You Ever Met an Old Person You Vibed With?” “People Watch, Southern Yoga and Nut Allergies” appears in descriptions of his work. The official line calls the comedy grounded and unpredictable.

Rowland made his late-night debut on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon in September 2022 and has performed on This Week at the Comedy Cellar. He plays Fred “Shred” Taylor on Animal Control, including the October 2026 episode “Tortoises & Turtlenecks.” His other appearances include Pause with Sam Jay, In the Minivan, and Stupid Questions with Chris DiStefano.

Rowland performs regularly in New York City and headlines clubs around the country.

shows.name: Michael Rowland (HBOmax, Late Night with Jimmy Fallon, Comedy Central) Headlines The Riot Comedy Club
Michael Rowland (HBOmax, Late Night with Jimmy Fallon, Comedy Central) Headlines The Riot Comedy Club

comedians.name: Mo Amer
comedians.profile_html:
In October 2026, Mo Amer sold out Radio City Music Hall. Dave Chappelle introduced him as a surprise guest; Jon Stewart, Ramy Youssef and Shane Gillis also appeared. The Houston Chronicle reported that Amer was the first Arab stand-up comedian to headline the roughly 6,000-seat room. “To switch gears and do my own show there and then have Dave go on there as a surprise guest, introduce me, it was so special man,” he later said.

Born in Kuwait to Palestinian parents, Amer arrived in Houston after his family fled the Gulf War and grew up in Alief. He started doing stand-up as a teenager in 1999. His Houston background runs through stories of family, citizenship, refugee experience and Texas.

His Netflix specials include Mo Amer: The Vagabond, 2021’s Mo Amer: Mohammed in Texas, and 2025’s Mo Amer: Wild World. He works in English, Arabic and Spanish, with Muslim and Arab American life at the center. “My mother is a gansta,” he says.

That material fed Mo, the Netflix comedy-drama he co-created, executive produced and stars in. Its second season arrived in January 2025. Amer also appeared on Hulu’s Ramy and joined WTF with Marc Maron, Episode 1619 in 2025.

comedians.name: Nikki Glaser
comedians.profile_html:
In September 2026, after transgender influencer Briel Adams-Wheatley publicly objected to an onstage joke, Nikki Glaser apologized privately and said she would remove it immediately. “I HATE anti trans jokes of all kinds, and to think I may have added to that rhetoric is disgusting to me,” she said.

Glaser began doing stand-up in college in 2002 after growing up in the St. Louis area. Her specials, from 2016’s Nikki Glaser: Perfect to the 2024 HBO/Max hour Nikki Glaser: Someday You’ll Die, cover sex, dating, sobriety, beauty, aging and death. In a 2023 Salon interview, she said, “I’m always trying to keep it very real.”

Glaser created, hosted and executive produced Comedy Central’s Not Safe with Nikki Glaser, then hosted and executive produced Max’s dating series FBoy Island. She hosted Saturday Night Live in November 2025 and the Golden Globe Awards in 2025 and 2026. Her Hulu special Nikki Glaser: Good Girl premiered in April 2026. The Stunning Tour launched that year.

comedians.name: Pauly Shore
comedians.profile_html:
Pauly Shore grew up around The Comedy Store, where his parents were comedian Sammy Shore and owner Mitzi Shore. He began performing stand-up at 17. In March 2026, on Felipe Esparza’s What’s Up Fool? Podcast, Shore discussed a Richard Simmons biopic, a memoir called How’d You Expect Me to Turn Out, and a 2026 stand-up tour.

Shore became an MTV VJ in 1989 and hosted Totally Pauly. His California stoner-surfer character, “The Weasel,” moved into the 1992 HBO special Pauly Does Dallas and the Showtime specials Pauly Shore’s Vegas Is My Oyster and Pauly Shore’s Pauly~tics. The act draws on San Fernando Valley slang, sex, partying, and MTV nostalgia.

On Fox’s Pauly, he played Pauly Sherman. Minding the Store followed his efforts to revive his acting career and run The Comedy Store. He appeared as himself on Workaholics and Hell’s Kitchen. In 2025, The PMS Podcast Show featured guests including David Lucas and Harland Williams. In 2026, Shore appeared on HATE TO BREAK IT TO YA with Jamie Kennedy.

Live, Shore leaves room for audience questions and crowd work. A January 2025 Pollstar review described a Boca Raton set built on recognition-driven laughs and a largely Gen X crowd.

comedians.name: Phil Hanley
comedians.profile_html:
Phil Hanley grew up in Oshawa, Ontario, struggled with reading from first grade, and was eventually diagnosed with dyslexia. Before stand-up, he worked as a runway model in Europe, then started doing open mics in Vancouver music venues. His 2025 memoir, Spellbound: My Life as a Dyslexic Wordsmith, includes the line, “I always prayed I’d wake up smart.”

His 2022 YouTube special, Ooh La La, calls him “a acid eating, dyslexic, former model who falls in love too easily.” He also has a 2015 Comedy Central special, The Half Hour: Phil Hanley, and credits including The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Late Night with Seth Meyers, and two episodes of Inside Amy Schumer.

A Comedy Cellar regular in New York, Hanley works in traditional jokes, audience interaction, and improvisation. The material is reflective, sharply observed, and rarely interested in making the point gently.

comedians.name: Reem Edan
comedians.profile_html:
In July 2026, on Arab Is Me, Reem Edan summed up her résumé: “all these credits and still no husband.” The episode covered Iraqi-American identity, dating, parents, social-media work, Arab and Muslim women’s expectations, and her Dry Bar Comedy special Ethnic, Ambiguous & Single.

Edan grew up in Fort Collins, Colorado, then lived in Bahrain after moving there shortly before September 11, 2001. Before comedy, she worked in film marketing and publicity connected with Paramount and Disney. In a New Arab interview, she said open mics and the question of what made her happy led her out of that work.

Her material takes on Iraqi-American and first-generation identity, Muslim upbringing, religion, family, immigrant parents, dating, cross-cultural expectations, and social media. Bits include “I’m Muslim Unless Trump Gets Elected,” “How To Talk Back To Aunties,” and “Chad GPT.”

Edan also does character-driven sketches. Her official biography credits a performance in Arabic on Shahid VIP’s The Stand Up Sketch Show. IMDb lists her as Reem and credits sketch characters in the 2025 series Great Job News!.

comedians.name: Sarper Güven
comedians.profile_html:
In September 2026, after the 90 Day: The Last Resort Season 3 tell-all, Sarper Güven confirmed that he and Shekinah had separated. A CinemaBlend report linked the split to their public dispute over his stand-up material. “To make it clear, we have been separated for at least eight months since the beginning of 2026,” he said. “In my heart and in my mind, I am SINGLE now.”

Turkish-born and from Istanbul, Güven joined 90 Day Fiancé: The Other Way with Shekinah in Season 5, introduced by TLC as a model and personal trainer. He returned for Season 6, then moved from Turkey to Los Angeles for 90 Day Fiancé Season 11. In 2025, he began pursuing stand-up in the United States, drawing material from marriage, immigrant life, and the cultural gap between Turkey and America.

Güven combines Turkish-style connected storytelling with shorter American jokes. He cites Sebastian Maniscalco’s physical performance as an influence but says he does not want to resemble anybody else. The act stays positive, high-energy, and more family-friendly than dark comedy. In a New Noise Magazine interview, he put the method plainly: “Every show I try three or four new jokes, that’s my style.” He tests material through audience interaction while working through hour-plus sets. On the September 8, 2026 episode of UnAuthorized Opinions, he discussed his comedy tour, television fame, marriage, and Turkish-versus-American cultural differences.

comedians.name: Tony Hinchcliffe
comedians.profile_html:
On The Joe Rogan Experience #2522 in July 2026, Tony Hinchcliffe discussed the backlash to his George Floyd joke from The Roast of Kevin Hart. “I’m going to go for it,” he said.

Hinchcliffe grew up in Youngstown, Ohio, and graduated from Ursuline High School in 2003. A December 2007 Vindicator profile found him in Los Angeles, working restaurant jobs and getting onstage at open mics. He later worked at The Comedy Store and wrote for Comedy Central’s The Burn with Jeff Ross and roast episodes involving James Franco, Justin Bieber, and Rob Lowe.

His solo specials include Netflix’s 2016 release One Shot and 2021’s Making Friends, uploaded to YouTube. Netflix released Kill Tony: Kill or Be Killed in April 2025, followed by the solo special Man of the People in June 2026.

He is closely associated with Kill Tony, the touring podcast where aspiring comics perform one-minute sets before improvised interviews and critiques from Hinchcliffe and a guest panel. He has called it “the most spontaneous and improvised show that is out there.”
